title: Pattern Headings: Groups of Literary Authors
summary: Pattern-heading list for groups of literary authors (pattern heading Authors, English). Subdivisions are free-floating under headings for groups of literary authors, including those with adjectival qualifiers (Dramatists, French; Women novelists), but not under individual authors (H 1110) or [...] literature--[...] authors headings (H 1156). The H 1100 classes-of-persons list also applies. Period subdivisions are not used when the heading is subdivided geographically; topical/form subdivisions may follow period subdivisions.
validation_rules: Subdivisions on this list are free-floating under headings for groups of literary authors, including groups with adjectival qualifiers (e.g. *Authors*; *Dramatists*; *Novelists*; *Poets*; *African American authors*; *Dramatists, French*; *Women novelists*; *Blind poets*). (H 1155.2, Types of heading covered)
Do not use this list under names of individual literary authors (use H 1110). (H 1155.2, Types of heading covered)
Do not use this list under headings of the type *[ . . . ] literature--[ . . . ] authors*; those represent bodies of literature (cf. H 1156). (H 1155.2, Types of heading covered)
Subdivisions from H 1100 (classes of persons) may also be used under groups of literary authors where there is no conflict. (H 1155.2, Relation to H 1100)

General headings for groups of literary authors (e.g. *Authors*; *Novelists*; *Women poets*; *Men authors*) need not be subdivided geographically, since nationality, ethnicity, language, or location is expressed by adjectival qualifiers. (H 1155.2, Note)

Period subdivisions: `--Old English, ca. 450-1100`; `--Middle English, 1100-1500`; `--Early modern, 1500-1700`; `--18th century`; `--19th century`; `--20th century`; `--21st century`. (H 1155.2, Period subdivisions)
Do not use a period subdivision under a heading for a group of literary authors that has a geographic subdivision. (H 1155.2, Period subdivisions note)

The topical and form subdivisions on this list (and appropriate H 1100 subdivisions) may follow a period subdivision, e.g. *Authors, [ . . . ]--[period subdivision]--Political and social views*. (H 1155.2, Topical and form subdivisions)
Only `--Political activity` on this list may be subdivided geographically. (H 1155.2, list)
`--Chronology` is a form subdivision ($v); it may also be used as $x for works about the form. (H 1155.2; H 1075 sec. 1.d)

[LC practice] Establish new subdivisions under *Authors, English* if possible; otherwise under the heading appropriate for the work; individual proposals may be needed for period subdivisions before the 18th century when the English pattern cannot be followed. (H 1155.2, New subdivisions)
[LC practice] If an exceptional variant form is retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating subdivision form (H 195); otherwise propose a change (H 193). (H 1155.2, Conflicts)

sections.heading: Types of heading covered by the pattern
sections.text:
Headings for groups of literary authors, including groups established with adjectival qualifiers. Examples: *Authors*; *Dramatists*; *Novelists*; *Poets*; *African American authors*; *Dramatists, French*; *Women novelists*; *Blind poets*. The category does not include names of individual literary authors, which are covered by H 1110. The category also does not include headings of the type [ . . . ] literature--[ . . . ] authors. These headings represent subordinate bodies of literature written by those author groups (cf. H 1156).

Note: Groups of literary authors are established with adjectival qualifiers to express nationality, ethnicity, publication language, or geographic location and are authorized for geographic subdivision. Therefore, it is not necessary to subdivide geographically the general headings for groups of literary authors, such as *Authors*; *Novelists*; *Women poets*; *Men authors*.

sections.heading: Relation to H 1100
sections.text: Subdivisions on the list of free-floating subdivisions used under classes of persons, H 1100, may also be used under headings for groups of literary authors where there is no conflict. This list contains the additional subdivisions that are specific to literary authors.

sections.heading: Conflicts
sections.text:
Any subdivision listed here can be used as a free-floating subdivision under any heading belonging to the category if it is appropriate and no conflict exists in the subject authority file. Subject authority records may exist for headings employing variant phrases or subdivisions equivalent to subdivisions on this list.

LC practice: If an exceptional variant form is to be retained, make a UF reference from the equivalent free-floating subdivision form following the procedures in H 195 if the reference does not yet exist. Otherwise, submit a proposal to change the variant form along with all bibliographic records requiring correction following the procedures in H 193.

sections.heading: New subdivisions
sections.text: Establish new subdivisions under *Authors, English*, if possible. If the subdivision would not be appropriate under the pattern heading, establish it under the heading appropriate for the work cataloged. Individual proposals may be necessary for period subdivisions before the 18th century when the English pattern cannot be followed.

sections.heading: Period subdivisions
sections.text:
Note: Do not use period subdivisions under headings for groups of literary authors with geographic subdivisions.

- `$y Old English, ca. 450-1100`
- `$y Middle English, 1100-1500`
- `$y Early modern, 1500-1700`
- `$y 18th century`
- `$y 19th century`
- `$y 20th century`
- `$y 21st century`

sections.heading: Topical and form subdivisions
sections.text:
Note: Most form subdivisions coded $v in this list may also be used as topical subdivisions coded $x when assigned to works about the form (see H 1075, sec. 1.d.).

The subdivisions below, as well as appropriate subdivisions from H 1100, may also be used under headings of the type Authors, [ . . . ]--[period subdivision].

- `$x Aesthetics`
- `$v Chronology`
- `$x Philosophy`
- `$x Political activity` (May Subd Geog)
- `$x Political and social views`
- `$x Relations with men`
- `$x Relations with women`
